## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ārāmadūsakajātaka* (Ja 268) is a canonical birth story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [catalog record; SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha recounted this discourse while staying in the countryside near Dakkhiṇagiri, taking the son of a gardener as the occasion for the instruction [SuttaCentral]. 

In the canonical identification of births (*samodhāna*) that concludes the tale, the Buddha reveals that the chief of the monkeys in the past life was reborn as the park-spoiling lad (*ārāmadūsakakumāra*), whereas the wise man (*paṇḍitapurisa*) who observed the scene was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1879]. In the standard editorial arrangement of the collection, the text directly precedes the *Sujātajātaka* [Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral lists four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse queries generated by DharmaNexus indicate no significant Pali-internal textual parallels and no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records early cross-tradition parallels for this specific Jātaka [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
